title: A ring-object cocone over a filtered diagram is a colimit when its underlying cocone is
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category], and let $I$ be a small filtered category: $I$ is nonempty, for any two objects $i,j$ there are arrows $i\to k$ and $j\to k$ to some object $k$, and for any two parallel arrows $u,v\colon i\to j$ there is an arrow $w\colon j\to k$ with $wu=wv$. Assume that for every object $Y$ of $\mathcal C$ both functors $Y\otimes-$ and $-\otimes Y$ preserve colimits of $I$-indexed diagrams [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Let $D\colon I\to\operatorname{Mon}(\mathcal C)$ be a diagram of ring objects of $\mathcal C$ and morphisms of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Let $A$ be a ring object and let $c_i\colon D(i)\to A$ $(i\in I)$ be morphisms of ring objects with $c_j\circ D(u)=c_i$ for every arrow $u\colon i\to j$. Suppose that $(A,(c_i)_{i\in I})$ is a colimit in $\mathcal C$ of the underlying diagram $i\mapsto D(i)$. Then $(A,(c_i)_{i\in I})$ is a colimit of $D$ in the category of ring objects of $\mathcal C$. Explicitly: if $B$ is a ring object and $b_i\colon D(i)\to B$ are morphisms of ring objects with $b_j\circ D(u)=b_i$ for every $u\colon i\to j$, then the unique morphism $b\colon A\to B$ of $\mathcal C$ with $b\circ c_i=b_i$ for all $i$ is a morphism of ring objects.

If moreover $\mathcal C$ is braided and $A$ and all $D(i)$ are commutative ring objects, then $(A,(c_i)_{i\in I})$ is also a colimit of $D$ in the full subcategory of commutative ring objects.

proof.text: Fix a ring object $B$ and a compatible ring-object cocone $(b_i:D(i)\to B)$. Forgetting its ring structure gives a cocone in $\mathcal C$. The assumed underlying colimit and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] give a unique morphism $b:A\to B$ such that $b\circ c_i=b_i$ for all $i$. We will verify the two defining equations for a ring-object morphism. Composition below is ordinary right-to-left composition.

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit: existence and uniqueness of the mediating morphism; applied to the underlying cocone.

proof.text: Write $\eta_R:\mathbf1\to R$ and $\mu_R:R\otimes R\to R$ for the unit and multiplication of any ring object $R$, as in [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Since $I$ is nonempty, choose an object $i$. Both $c_i$ and $b_i$ preserve units, so $b\circ\eta_A=b\circ c_i\circ\eta_{D(i)}=b_i\circ\eta_{D(i)}=\eta_B$. This proves unit preservation.

source.place: Third isomorphism: elementary unit check in the ring-object upgrade; nonemptiness is Stacks Tag 002V, definition-directed.

proof.text: Set $f=b\circ\mu_A$ and $g=\mu_B\circ(b\otimes b)$, both maps $A\otimes A\to B$. For each $k\in I$, preservation of multiplication by $c_k,b_k$, the equation $b\circ c_k=b_k$, and bifunctoriality of tensor give $f\circ(c_k\otimes c_k)=b\circ c_k\circ\mu_{D(k)}=b_k\circ\mu_{D(k)}=\mu_B\circ(b_k\otimes b_k)=g\circ(c_k\otimes c_k)$. These are equations of morphisms, requiring no interpretation as elements of the objects.

source.place: Third isomorphism: elementary check of multiplication on two inputs from the same stage; tensor bifunctor laws are Stacks Tag 0FFK, definition-monoidal-category.

proof.text: For arbitrary objects $i,j\in I$, choose $k$ and arrows $u:i\to k$, $v:j\to k$, using filteredness as written in the statement and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The cocone equations and tensor bifunctoriality give $c_i\otimes c_j=(c_k\otimes c_k)\circ(D(u)\otimes D(v))$. Precomposing the equality of step 3 with $D(u)\otimes D(v)$ therefore gives $f\circ(c_i\otimes c_j)=g\circ(c_i\otimes c_j)$ for every pair $i,j$. No equalization of parallel arrows is needed for this calculation.

source.place: Tag 002V, definition-directed, common successor condition; Tag 0FFK, definition-monoidal-category, tensor as a bifunctor. Elementary expansion of the blueprint third isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix $i$. By the assumed preservation of $I$-indexed colimits by $D(i)\otimes-$, the cocone with vertex $D(i)\otimes A$ and legs $\mathrm{id}_{D(i)}\otimes c_j$ is a colimit of $j\mapsto D(i)\otimes D(j)$. Here preservation means precisely that the image of a colimit cocone is a colimit cocone. The maps $f\circ(c_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_A)$ and $g\circ(c_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_A)$ agree after each such leg by step 4 and bifunctoriality. They are thus two mediating morphisms for the same cocone, so uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] makes them equal.

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit, uniqueness applied to the cocone preserved by D(i) tensor -; Tag 0FFK, definition-monoidal-category. Elementary expansion of the blueprint third isomorphism.

proof.text: By the assumed preservation of $I$-indexed colimits by $-\otimes A$, the cocone with vertex $A\otimes A$ and legs $c_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_A$ is a colimit of $i\mapsto D(i)\otimes A$. Step 5 says that $f$ and $g$ agree after all its legs. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $f=g$, that is, $b\circ\mu_A=\mu_B\circ(b\otimes b)$. Along with step 2 this is exactly the definition of a morphism of ring objects in [sk-def-sfb-ring-object].

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit, uniqueness applied to the cocone preserved by - tensor A; ring-object morphism definition from the blueprint sk-def-sfb-ring-object. Elementary expansion of the third isomorphism.

proof.text: The ring-object morphism $b$ has the required factorization equations by step 1. Any other ring-object morphism with these equations has the same underlying morphism by the underlying colimit uniqueness, hence is equal to $b$: a ring-object morphism is just a morphism satisfying the multiplication and unit equations. This proves the ring-object colimit universal property. In the braided case, let $B$ be any commutative ring object. The same $b$ is a morphism in the full subcategory of commutative ring objects, because fullness means that its morphisms are exactly the ring-object morphisms between these objects. The existence and uniqueness just proved therefore give the final asserted colimit as well.

source.place: Third isomorphism: ring-object universal property and its restriction to the full subcategory of commutative ring objects.
